comment: A made-up mini translation for the Bible page's stub (scripture routes in routes/bible.mjs). Book names are real; every verse is invented.
phrases: The lantern keeper walked the quiet road at dawn
and the orchard gate stood open to every traveller
A small boat rested where the river bends toward the hills
the bread was shared at the long table in the evening
Snow settled on the roofs of the harbour town
and the children sang beside the old stone well
The weaver counted the threads and found none missing
a bright star hung over the sleeping valley
The gardener planted cedar seeds along the northern wall
and the bells rang twice when the morning came
Wind moved over the barley fields like a slow tide
the shepherd's lamp burned steady through the long night

PSA 23: The lantern keeper guards the quiet road; no traveller goes without a light.
He sets a table in the green meadow and fills the clay jars by the slow stream.
He mends the torn sail and steers the small boat home along the straight channel.
Even when fog lies thick in the low valley I am not afraid, for the keeper's lamp is near; his staff and his lantern steady me.
He lays out bread before the long winter and pours warm cider until the cup runs over.
Kindness will walk beside me through every season, and I will rest in the keeper's house as long as the lamps are lit.

JHN 3.16: The weaver gave her finest cloth to the whole village, so that no one who came to her door would go cold in winter.
JHN 3.17: She did not come to count their faults but to mend what was torn.
JHN 3.18: Whoever takes the cloth is kept warm; whoever turns it away stays in the cold of their own choosing.
